not_rules.quote:
The parliaments of all states except Qld are ‘bicameral’. This means parliament has 2 chambers or houses:

- the Legislative Council – also called the ‘upper house’
- the Legislative Assembly (NSW, Vic and WA) or House of Assembly (SA and Tas) – also called the ‘lower house’.
The parliaments of Qld, the ACT and the NT are ‘unicameral’. This means parliament has one chamber or house – the Legislative Assembly.
The choice of 'MLA' or 'MP' for members of state and territory parliaments is less clear-cut.

covers.quote: Address certain office holders of the Australian Parliament as ‘Honourable’

The President of the Senate and the Speaker of the House of Representatives (the presiding officers) use the title ‘Honourable’.
‘Honourable’ is also given to members of the Australian Parliament who are:

tags.violation_condition: failing to address mayors outside capital cities according to their designated form ('The Right Worshipful...' for Geelong/Newcastle/Wollongong, or 'His/Her Worship...' for other cities)

when: mayors of Geelong, Newcastle and Wollongong use 'The Right Worshipful the [Lord] Mayor of [city]'
mayors of other cities use 'His' or 'Her Worship the Mayor of [city]'
in correspondence: open with 'Dear Mayor' (or 'Dear Lord Mayor' if applicable) and conclude with 'Yours faithfully'
rules.why: G-1, G-2: Consolidates mayoral styling for cities outside capital cities.

anchor.quote: Address a shire president as ‘President [family name]’. The abbreviation for ‘President’ is ‘Pres’ without a full stop, but use the full title ‘President’ because it’s clearer.

covers.quote: Address an alderman (regardless of gender) as ‘Alderman[family name]’. The abbreviation for ‘Alderman’ is ‘Ald’ without a full stop.
Address a councillor as ‘Councillor [family name]’. The abbreviation for ‘Councillor’ is ‘Cr’ without a full stop.

parts.quote: President Smith
Alderman Miller
Ald Miller
Councillor Brown
Cr Brown

tags.violation_condition: using an abbreviation with a full stop or failing to address shire presidents, aldermen, or councillors by their correct title prefix ('President', 'Alderman'/'Ald', or 'Councillor'/'Cr')

when: address a shire president as 'President [family name]'; prefer full title 'President' over 'Pres'
address an alderman as 'Alderman [family name]' or 'Ald [family name]' without a full stop
address a councillor as 'Councillor [family name]' or 'Cr [family name]' without a full stop
in formal correspondence: open with 'Dear President', 'Dear Alderman' or 'Dear Councillor' and conclude with 'Yours faithfully'
in less formal correspondence: open with 'Dear President', 'Dear Alderman' or 'Dear Councillor [family name]' and conclude with 'Yours sincerely'
rules.why: G-1, G-2: Consolidates local government representatives (presidents, aldermen, councillors) into one rule.
